standard_prerequisites.name: Generation of the positive part as an ideal

core_obligations: One direction: if the f_i generate S as an algebra over S_0, then every positive-degree element is a polynomial without constant term in the f_i, so the positive part is generated by them as an ideal (proof lines 14006-14008).

For the converse, prove by induction on the degree that every homogeneous element is a polynomial in the f_i with coefficients in S_0: for positive degree write it as a sum of multiples of the f_i, replace the coefficients by their homogeneous components of the complementary degree, and apply the induction hypothesis (proof lines 14009-14016).
proof_roadmap: Read off ideal generation from polynomial generation in one direction (proof lines 14005-14008).
Do an induction on degree using homogeneity of the coefficients in the other (proof lines 14008-14017).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that homogeneous elements of positive degree generate a graded ring over its degree-zero part as an algebra exactly when they generate the positive-degree part as an ideal (statement lines 13998-14003). The proof does not compare the two filtered pieces abstractly: one direction reads polynomial generation without constant term, and the other inducts on the degree of a homogeneous element, writing it as a sum of multiples of the generators and using gradedness to replace each coefficient by its homogeneous component of the complementary degree before applying the induction hypothesis (proof lines 14005-14017). That degree bookkeeping on the coefficients is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
